title: Evict Yourself For This Bugatti
tagline: Finally embracing poverty? Good, you're ready for the *last* Bugatti Bolide. Imagine: you're late on rent (again), but you pull up to the eviction notice in *this*. Your landlord? Speechless. Your bank account? Weeping. Just remember, ramen noodles taste better when you're eating them in a multi-million dollar car. Priorities, people. Priorities.

title: GT40: Because Rent Is Overrated
tagline: Finally, a way to impress your ex-wife's new boyfriend! Sure, you'll be eating ramen for the next decade, but who needs food when you're cruising in a classic Ford GT40? Just imagine the look on his face when you pull up to the courthouse for your next custody battle. Assuming, of course, you haven't sold it for bail money by then.

title: Divorce Papers Included (Probably)
tagline: So, you've decided that crippling debt is *exactly* what your mid-life crisis needs? This 1980 Porsche Safari says, "I'm running from my problems... at 80 miles an hour... through a sand dune." Guaranteed to impress absolutely no one but that one guy at the gas station who also peaked in high school. Enjoy explaining this to your therapist. And your soon-to-be ex-wife.

title: The Boat's Personal Bodyguard
tagline: For when your yacht's self-esteem can't handle another ding. This is the marine equivalent of a security detail for your vessel. Perfect for the paranoid sailor who thinks every dock is a potential threat. Now you can sleep soundly knowing your boat's hull is protected from the judgmental stares of other boats.

title: Divorce? Get a Snowdog!
tagline: So, you've finally snapped and decided to abandon your family ski trip halfway up the mountain. Good for you! But how will you drag your shame (and your gear) back down? Enter the SnowdogX. Because nothing says 'I regret everything' like dropping seven grand on a personal snow-towing machine instead of, you know, therapy. Enjoy your newfound freedom...and crippling debt!

title: Dirt Bike for Overcompensators
tagline: Because nothing says 'I'm totally secure in my masculinity' like a $23k ATV that can outrun your existential dread. Perfect for the suburban dad who needs to prove he's still relevant during his monthly off-road therapy session with the guys. Just don't ask about the payment plan.

title: Buggy for Bugs
tagline: When your off-road adventures involve dodging dragonflies and navigating through mosquito swarms, the Libelule All Terrain Vehicle is your six-legged savior. Perfect for entomologists who refuse to sacrifice comfort for their insect-chasing pursuits or suburbanites tired of mowing the lawn—just let this buggy do the work while you sip your lemonade.

title: Back... to the Showroom?
tagline: So, you're telling me I can *finally* relive my glory days of awkwardly hitting on the barista at the cafe, but this time, with the added bonus of silent electric propulsion? Perfect for stealthily arriving at the next 80's themed karaoke night. Just try not to accidentally invent the internet while you're there.

title: Grandpa's E-Bike
tagline: For when you want to feel like a rebellious teen on a paper route, but with the stability of a walker. Perfect for cruising to the senior center in style, or when you need to outpace your grandkids on the way to the ice cream truck. Just don't expect to keep up with the neighborhood's electric scooter gang.

title: Zombie Apocalypse? No Problem.
tagline: For when your car dies in the middle of nowhere and your phone has 1% battery. This little guy is the difference between a romantic moonlit walk home and a terrifying encounter with a raccoon named Jeff. Fits in your glove box, so you can forget about it until you absolutely need it. Like that emergency chocolate stash.

title: Tiny Tractor of Terror
tagline: For when your backyard is too small for a real ATV but too big for a toddler’s tricycle. Perfect for mowing your lawn while pretending you’re in a Mad Max prequel. Just don’t blame us if your neighbors start calling you ‘The Mini Menace.’

title: Bond’s Grocery Getaway
tagline: When your weekly Whole Foods run needs a 0-60 in 3.4 seconds, this is the cart. Perfect for dodging organic kale enthusiasts or making a dramatic exit after forgetting your reusable bags. Just don’t try to fit a week’s worth of avocados in the trunk—it’s a coupe, not a Costco shuttle.

title: Divorce Papers Delivery System
tagline: Finally, a drone powerful enough to deliver your crippling debt directly to your doorstep. Or, I guess, ferry emergency supplies during the apocalypse. But let's be real, you're gonna use this $12,500 behemoth to avoid eye contact with your ex while serving them divorce papers from the sky. Because therapy is expensive, but apparently this isn't?

title: Road Trip Regret Bin
tagline: For when your backseat becomes a biohazard zone. This trash can won't topple, even when your kid tosses a half-eaten McNugget at it like a grenade. Perfect for the parent who's given up on cleanliness but still clings to hope. Fits in cupholders, because nothing says 'family road trip' like a trash can in your coffee spot.

title: The Bicycle That Fits in Your Backpack (Maybe)
tagline: Perfect for the urban commuter who's also a part-time spy. Folds up so small, you can hide it in your trench coat while you sneak into that 'employees only' elevator. Just don't try to fit it in your backpack—unless you're willing to sacrifice your lunch. At $2,375, it's not cheap, but hey, at least it won't get stolen from your bike rack.

title: Road Rage Apocalypse Buggy
tagline: So, your therapist finally convinced you to embrace your inner child? Great, now you can terrorize suburban cul-de-sacs in this lunar-lander-meets-monster-truck fever dream. Perfect for escaping the impending societal collapse or just aggressively retrieving your kid's soccer ball from the neighbor's yard. Just remember, therapy doesn't cover vehicular manslaughter. We're all doomed, anyway.

title: Divorce Papers Included (Yacht)
tagline: Finally, a boat big enough to house all your regrets! Imagine: You're on this obscenely large yacht, sipping champagne, while your ex is stuck with the dinghy. Perfect for when you need to dramatically sail away from all your responsibilities... and your crippling student loan debt. Because let's be honest, if you're buying this, you're definitely declaring bankruptcy next year.

title: The Turbo Snail of '87
tagline: For the guy who wants to pretend he's in a Fast & Furious movie but actually just needs to impress his book club. This Buick GNX is the perfect blend of 'I have money' and 'I don't know what to do with it.' It's like a grandpa's car that somehow got a caffeine addiction. Just don't ask about the gas mileage.

title: Bike or Scooter? Why Not Both?
tagline: Tired of your bike's identity crisis? This two-wheeled chameleon switches from pedal power to scooter mode faster than you can say 'why did I buy this?' Perfect for the urbanite who wants to feel like a kid on a scooter one moment and a serious cyclist the next. Just don't try to do a wheelie in either mode—you'll regret it.

title: Snowzilla: Your ATV’s Winter Makeover
tagline: Because nothing says 'I’m prepared for winter' like turning your ATV into a snowmobile. Perfect for the over-enthusiastic off-roader who refuses to let a little snow ruin their weekend. Now you can plow through powder like a boss—or at least until you realize you forgot to bring extra gas.

title: Therapist? Nah, I Got Tanks.
tagline: Aggressively parallel park outside that HOA meeting. Or, perhaps you're just *really* committed to avoiding rush hour. Either way, this lightly-used Otokar lets everyone know your feelings about potholes...and probably zoning laws. Fuel efficiency? Debatable. Street cred? Immeasurable.

title: Outlier Megayacht: Divorce Incoming
tagline: So, your crypto scheme finally paid off? Congrats, you're officially insufferable. Now you need the Outlier Megayacht, because subtlety is for peasants. This floating palace will let you loudly broadcast your questionable life choices to everyone within a 5-mile radius. Go ahead, buy it. You deserve to be resented by the entire ocean.

title: Truck Bed Tetris
tagline: For the overachiever who needs to fit a small library, a dog, and a kayak in their truck bed—without the existential dread of a jigsaw puzzle. Modular, yes. Practical for your 'just in case' hoarding? Absolutely. Perfect for when your life requires more organization than your local IKEA.

title: Divorce In A Can (RV)
tagline: So, you wanna be homeless, but *glamping* homeless? This expandable RV is perfect for alienating your spouse and driving aimlessly until you run out of gas money (and hope). Just picture it: arguing over counter space while hurtling down the highway at a cool 50mph. Because, let's be honest, if you're buying this, rational decisions are already a distant memory.

title: One-Wheel Wonder
tagline: For the urban commuter who wants to feel like they're riding a unicycle but without the clown suit. Perfect for dodging tourists in Times Square or when your bike's other wheel is in the shop for a 'check-up'. Just don't ask us how you're supposed to carry your groceries.

title: Anti-Gravity: For *Those* Commutes
tagline: Tired of sidewalks? Yeah, me too. This hoverboard promises sweet, sweet freedom from pedestrian laws. Imagine soaring over that perpetually congested crosswalk during rush hour. Just picture the looks on their faces as you silently float above their minivan-induced misery. (Note: May attract unwanted attention from local pigeons.)

title: Bronco for the 'I Forgot My Pants' Crowd
tagline: When your off-road adventure involves more mud puddles than actual trails, and you need to explain to your dog why you're wearing shorts in December, this 1969 Ford Bronco is your ticket. Perfect for the 'I thought this was a good idea at 2 AM' phase of life. Just don't ask about the fuel efficiency.

title: Buick Riviera: The Midlife Crisis Special
tagline: For when your divorce settlement came through and you need to make a statement, but also want to pretend you're still practical. This 1960s land yacht is the perfect blend of 'I've made it' and 'I'm still pretending to be a responsible adult.' It's like a convertible for people who want to feel the wind in their hair but also need a place to put their golf clubs.

title: Fast Cars, Faster Mistakes
tagline: For when your midlife crisis needs a professional co-pilot. Perfect for the person who’s tired of boring golf outings and wants to spin out in a Porsche instead. Bonus: The instructor’s sighs of disappointment are included in the price.

title: Divorce? Get an AIR POD!
tagline: So, your mid-life crisis mobile just isn't cutting it anymore? Need to escape the suburbs (and your crippling existential dread) *vertically*? The Rictor X4 Air Mobility Pod is here for you. Just picture yourself, soaring above traffic jams and alimony payments, finally free... until the FAA slaps you with a hefty fine for flying over a school zone. Enjoy bankruptcy!

title: Goodbye, Retirement Fund. Hello, Regret.
tagline: So, your mid-life crisis needs a turbo boost? Perfect. This hand-crafted, obscenely-priced speedster will let you relive your glory days (which probably involved questionable hair and even more questionable decisions). Just picture it: wind in your thinning hair, alimony payments bouncing, and the faint scent of impending bankruptcy. Enjoy!

title: Divorce? Buy a Unimog!
tagline: So, your spouse finally left you? Excellent! Now you have the perfect excuse to blow the settlement on this ridiculously overpriced Mercedes-Benz Unimog. Who needs therapy when you can crush Prius' under your six-wheeled monument to overcompensation? Sure, you'll be eating ramen for the next decade, but at least you'll arrive at the soup kitchen in *style.*

title: Vroom with the Rich
tagline: For when your midlife crisis needs a German accent. Test drive an Audi on a track, because nothing says 'I’ve made questionable life choices' like paying $600 to pretend you’re in a Fast & Furious sequel. Perfect for the guy who’s tired of speeding tickets and wants to feel like a race car driver—at least until he realizes he can’t parallel park.

title: Tiny Car Condo
tagline: For when your Matchbox collection graduates to a full-fledged fleet. This pop-up garage is perfect for the urban dweller who’s tired of their 1:18 scale Porsche getting trampled by roommates. Fits neatly on a desk, because even miniature cars deserve a penthouse.

title: Shotgun for the Over-Cautious
tagline: When you're convinced that one barrel just isn't enough to handle your neighbor's questionable BBQ skills or the sudden appearance of a rogue garden gnome, the DP-12 is here to double your peace of mind. Perfect for those who believe in the 'better safe than sorry' philosophy, especially when 'sorry' involves a lot of buckshot and a very loud point.

title: Behold! The Apocalypse BMW.
tagline: So, your therapist *insists* you need more 'outdoor time,' but the idea of actual nature makes you shudder? This WalzWerk X-Plorer is the answer. Cruise through a mild zombie outbreak in style, or, you know, just intimidate the Prius drivers at Whole Foods. Either way, you're winning.

title: Divorce Papers on Wheels
tagline: Finally, a way to blow 30 grand proving you're 'environmentally conscious' to your ex. Picture this: You, zipping past her Prius on this solid-state *thing*, hair whipping, fueled by pure spite and the vague promise of a slightly lower carbon footprint. The only thing green about this is the envy of your soon-to-be-bankrupt self.

title: Divorce? Buy. This. Tank.
tagline: So, you've finally snapped. The HOA sent you one too many passive-aggressive lawn care notices? The ex is demanding *more* alimony? Solution: the Rezvani Tank. Because when you're this close to societal collapse, nothing says 'I've given up' like driving a small house down Main Street. Just remember to factor in the cost of therapy...and bail.

title: Grandpa's War Rig
tagline: When your off-grid cabin needs a vehicle that’s seen more action than your dating life, this 1951 Willys M38 Jeep is your ticket. Perfect for hauling firewood while pretending you’re on a covert mission. Just don’t expect Bluetooth—this thing still runs on hope and duct tape.

title: Honk If You Love Corgis
tagline: For the individual who finds themselves weeping uncontrollably at dog videos while stuck in traffic. Now you can dab your tears with a tissue pulled directly from a fluffy corgi posterior. Because what better way to process existential dread than with canine-themed paper products?

title: The Yacht for People Who Hate Yachts
tagline: Imagine you're at a 'yacht party' but it's actually just you and your cat, because you're allergic to both people and fun. This is the boat for you. It's like a tiny apartment that floats, perfect for those who want to be alone but still want to brag about having a yacht. Bonus: it's small enough to fit in your garage, so you can finally fulfill your dream of being a pirate in your own driveway.

title: Rock Crawling Madness Ensues
tagline: For the friend who thinks hiking is boring, but watching RC cars climb rocks is thrilling. Spend hours building this kit, then immediately destroy it on a rocky terrain, because that's what friends are for.

title: Elon's Shopping Cart
tagline: When your suburban mom needs to haul both her yoga mat and her divorce papers in style. The Tesla Model Y: it’s like a Prius, but with more existential dread and a ‘Full Self-Driving’ mode that still can’t parallel park. Perfect for the eco-conscious parent who also wants to subtly remind their neighbors they’re ‘innovative.’

title: Yacht for Your Midlife Crisis
tagline: For when your therapist says 'maybe you should try sailing' instead of a third divorce. The Mylius M60GL is a sleek, carbon-fiber yacht that'll make you feel like a Bond villain—until you realize you're just ferrying your book club to the next brunch spot. Perfect for those who want to impress their ex while pretending they're not trying.

title: Solar Panels Ruin Your Truck!
tagline: Finally, a way to look even MORE ridiculous while tailgating! Slap these bad boys on your truck bed, and you'll be the envy of every redneck who's ALSO trying to offset their carbon footprint (while simultaneously chugging a twelve-pack). Because nothing says "eco-conscious" like a pickup truck with enough solar panels to power a small village. Prepare to be broke AND mocked.

title: Yacht-Sized Escape Pod, Anyone?
tagline: So, divorce is final, the house is gone, and your ex got the actual yacht. But you still have that sudden urge to be surrounded by water? This mini-yacht-capsule situation lets you bob peacefully in the marina, contemplating poor decisions and the surprisingly buoyant nature of regret.

title: Jetski Boat: Divorce Speedrun
tagline: Finally, a way to make everyone at the lake hate you even MORE. This jetski-boat hybrid is perfect for when you can't decide between aquatic personal injury and leisurely alcoholism. Picture it: you, Captain Buzzkill, slowly motoring around with seven of your closest frenemies, wishing you'd just stayed home. Go on, ruin everyone's summer. You deserve it.

title: Three Wheels to Bankruptcy!
tagline: So, your midlife crisis hit, but you're too eco-conscious for a gas-guzzling convertible. Enter: the electric trike of shame. Picture yourself, helmet hair flapping, desperately trying to outrun your alimony payments at a blistering 25mph. Yes, you could buy a sensible car, but where's the fun in fiscal responsibility? Just remember, ramen noodles pair well with crippling debt.

title: Muscle Car for Your Midlife Crisis
tagline: The perfect ride for when you realize your life choices have led you to a dead-end job and a divorce. This beast will make your neighbors question their life decisions as you peel out of your driveway at 6 AM, coffee in hand, ready to outrun your existential dread. Just don't ask about the gas mileage.

title: Hover-Kart: Sidewalk Speed Demon
tagline: Neighbors complaining about your hoverboard skills? Channel that reckless energy into something *slightly* less terrifying. This kit transforms your electric balance board into a low-riding go-kart. Perfect for silently terrorizing the local dog park or staging a dramatic, low-speed getaway from that awkward Tupperware party. Helmet not included (but strongly suggested).

title: Electric Lexus: WHY, THO?
tagline: So, you've finally accepted that your mid-life crisis needs an eco-friendly twist? Congrats, you're still insufferable, just quieter now. This Lexus LFA Concept EV is for the guy who loudly complains about gas prices while simultaneously Venmo requesting his kids for avocado toast money. Go ahead, trade that roaring V10 for the gentle hum of your impending divorce. We're sure it'll solve *all* your problems. (Spoiler: it won't.)

title: Bavarian Two-Wheeled Therapy
tagline: For when your midlife crisis needs a little more torque than a Harley. This BMW R Ninet 801 is the perfect antidote to suburban monotony—just imagine cruising through a German forest, the wind in your hair, and the faint smell of schnitzel in the air. Bonus: it’s the only thing that’ll make your neighbors jealous of your garage.

title: Vroom Vroom, I'm Bankrupt!
tagline: So, your mid-life crisis involves torching your savings on a car that looks like it was designed by a sentient cheese grater? Fantastic. Imagine pulling up to your ex's wedding in this thing, only to realize you can't afford gas because you blew it all on the down payment. Enjoy the walk home, sucker. At least you'll look…futuristic doing it?

title: Overpriced Van for Overlanders
tagline: Ever wanted to live in a van down by the river, but with a mortgage payment? The Winnebago Revel is your ticket to 'glamping' in a 4x4 with a kitchenette, perfect for that time you decide to drive to the middle of nowhere and realize you forgot to pack food. Because nothing says adventure like a $135k van with a built-in microwave.

title: Dad's Midlife Crisis on Wheels
tagline: For the man who wants to relive his 4x4 glory days without actually going off-road. Perfect for driving to the grocery store in style, or when you need to impress your neighbors by 'rescuing' their Prius from a 2-inch snowfall. Comes with enough cup holders to host a tailgate in your driveway.

title: Gotham's Rear End
tagline: For the Dark Knight in you, because your brake light needed a cape. Useful when you're tailgating a Joker-themed party bus.

title: The Bike That Fits in Your Backpack (Sort Of)
tagline: For the urban nomad who refuses to be tethered to a bike rack or a gym membership. This whippet folds up like a sad origami swan, perfect for stuffing into the overhead bin on your morning commute or hiding from your landlord who banned bikes in the hallway. Just don’t ask us how you’re supposed to pedal it while it’s folded.

title: Jeep's Overpriced Junk Drawer
tagline: Because your Wrangler’s cup holders can’t handle both your Yeti and that mysterious jar of pickled eggs from last summer’s tailgate. This trunk chest is the over-engineered solution for when you need to stash your extra fanny packs, spare glow sticks, and that one inflatable flamingo you refuse to leave at home. Just don’t ask why it costs more than your first car.

title: Tony Stark's Bad Idea
tagline: Because you want to yell 'I am Iron Man' at traffic lights, this helmet is perfect for the motorcyclist who's also a Marvel cosplayer on the side, or just really likes Arc Reactor-inspired headgear.

title: Broke Fast, Die Furious.
tagline: So, your therapist told you to find a 'healthy outlet' for your daddy issues? Look no further! For the price of a modest suburban home, you can own Paul Walker's actual Ford GT. Finally, you can LARP as Brian O'Conner while simultaneously dodging calls from your landlord. Just try not to wrap it around a tree... your *other* daddy will be furious.

title: Divorcee Starter Pack, German Edition
tagline: So, your spouse ran off with the artisanal cheesemaker? Perfect. This AMG SL Roadster is *precisely* what you need. Ditch the mini-van, crank the opera, and aggressively parallel park outside that overpriced therapist's office. Show them who's winning... or at least pretending really, really hard.

title: Sneaky Dirt Donut
tagline: For when you need to quietly escape your in-laws' ranch, this $7,500 electric ATV is your stealthy savior.

title: Car Savior in a Pinch
tagline: Because you never know when you'll need to cut a seatbelt or crack a window to escape your in-laws at a roadside attraction.

title: Scoot Like Nobody Watches
tagline: For when you need to impress your cat with a 15mph joyride down a deserted alley at 3am.

title: Vette Dreams Come True
tagline: For the enthusiast who needs a Corvette, but also a reminder of their failed West Coast dreams, this California Corvette concept is a nostalgic nightmare come true, perfect for cruising to your therapist's office.

title: Bony Ride Accessories
tagline: Because your bike was missing a hint of mortality, these skull valve caps bring a touch of edginess to your daily commute, or that one weird cousin's birthday party.

title: Crash Less, Spend More!
tagline: Finally, glasses for when your mid-life crisis involves illegally street racing your minivan at 3 AM. These HD night driving glasses promise to turn the blurry abyss into… slightly less blurry abyss. Because apparently, seeing *something* before you plow into that mailbox is worth $22. Go ahead, order 'em. Your insurance agent totally won't judge.

title: Jaguar for Your Desk
tagline: Because your office needs a mid-century crisis, this E-Type concept model is perfect for the coworker who still thinks it's 1961.

tagline: For when you need to escape the in-laws on a camping trip, but still want to arrive in something that screams 'I have a midlife crisis, but also a decent 4x4 system'.

title: Ridiculous Desk Racer
tagline: For when you're stuck in a meeting and your mind wanders to Le Mans, this V8 Daytona GT model brings the thrill of racing to your stagnant office desk, because who needs productivity?

title: Vintage Pony Up
tagline: For the enthusiast who needs a 302 Quadra in their life, like a mid-project restoration of a '97 Mustang, because why settle for a working car?

title: Farmhand on Autopilot
tagline: For when you need to mow the north field, but your tractor-driving uncle is still asleep from last night's bingo.

title: Divorce-Mobile: Nature Edition
tagline: So, your spouse hates your taste in everything? Excellent. This Bailey Discovery camper lets you 'discover' just how much you enjoy solitude. Picture this: You, a lukewarm can of beans, and the deafening silence of the great outdoors. Tell me that isn't living.

title: Retro Revival Ride
tagline: For when you want to relive the 90s, but your flannel shirt isn't enough, this Nissan Z Proto Coupe is the answer to all your nostalgic prayers, or a midlife crisis – we won't judge.

title: Jeep's Secret Shame Stash
tagline: Paranoid someone's eyeing your emergency tire chains? This vault lets you hide them *inside* your Jeep. Because nothing says 'prepared for the apocalypse' like a locked box full of jumper cables only *you* know about. Perfect for those who trust their vehicle, but not society.

title: Sneaky Bike Alert
tagline: For when you want to silently judge your neighbor's lawn care habits from a distance, this electric road bike is perfect. Cruise by at 4am, unnoticed, and ponder life's mysteries.

tagline: For the person who needs a $100k car to drive to their secret underground lair, the 2026 BMW M2 CS is a solid choice, mostly because it's fast enough to escape the judgmental looks from pedestrians.

title: Trailer for the Truly Extra

title: Three Wheels of Chaos

title: Dead Car? Panic Button

title: Bling for Your Bike
tagline: Because your motorcycle wasn't visible from space, add these LED lights. Now you can blind fellow drivers while riding at dusk, ensuring they remember your flashy exit from the highway.

title: Sun Powered Guilt Trip
tagline: For the eco-warrior who needs an SUV to haul their compost bin, this solar SUV is a weirdly practical choice for a rural music festival escape.

tagline: For the urban hermit who needs to escape their studio apartment, but not the crippling rent, this eBike is a pricey freedom machine. Imagine zooming away from responsibilities at 28mph.

tagline: Because who needs human interaction on a road trip? This Mercedes camper van is perfect for solo adventures, or when you want to escape your family at the campsite.

title: Farm Truck on Steroids
tagline: For the farmer who needs to haul livestock and a hint of German engineering arrogance, this Unimog is perfect. Imagine driving it to the local farmer's market, just to fetch some artisanal kale.

title: Dead Car Savior

title: Floating Midlife Crisis (Aquila 36)
tagline: For when you've given up on land, but still want to impress your neighbors from afar, comes the Aquila 36 Power Catamaran, because who needs a backyard when you can have a bow?

title: Bike Seat: Safety First?
tagline: For the cyclist who's already wearing a helmet, elbow pads, and reflective vest... but still feels naked. This bicycle seat belt is perfect for reenacting your daily commute in your living room. Finally, that extra level of security you crave while stationary!

title: Divorce Your Wallet, Ride Safe!
tagline: So, you're telling me I can drop $1400 on a helmet that *might* prevent permanent brain damage, but *definitely* guarantees I'll be eating ramen for the next six months? Perfect for the guy who values his skull more than his electric bill. Just imagine: you're crashing your motorcycle, listening to smooth jazz, and thinking, 'Well, at least my head's insured... against *impact*, not crippling debt.'

title: Broke? Now You're Speeding!

Perfect for those late-night existential crisis drives to the 24-hour bodega for discount ice cream. Sure, you'll be sleeping in your car, but at least you'll be doing it in *style*... if you can afford the gas. Good luck with that.

title: Behold! The Automotive Pancake
tagline: Ever fantasize about being intimately acquainted with your engine? This foldable topside creeper lets you hover directly over the abyss, wrench in hand. Perfect for when you absolutely *must* diagnose that subtle ticking sound while contemplating the fragility of existence... and avoiding back strain.

title: Crotch Rocket, Meet Debt Rocket
tagline: So, you've always dreamed of outrunning your crippling student loan debt? This CFMoto V4 SR-RR Motorcycle is here to help (maybe). Picture this: You're screaming down the highway at 180mph, wind in your hair, repossession notice flapping uselessly behind you. Freedom! Until you realize you also can't afford gas. Worth it? Probably not. Will you buy it anyway? Absolutely.

title: WaveRunner for the Win
tagline: Because your lake vacation wasn't complete without a jet-powered divorce from your wallet and a near-death experience with a rogue buoy.

title: Trunk Trash Tamer
tagline: For when you've got a car full of fast food wrappers and last week's gym clothes, this mesh organizer is the adulting hack you need to pretend your life is together.

title: Tailgate Party Enabler
tagline: For when you need a desk, a bench, and a makeshift bar at the rural music festival, but your truck's bed is already full of questionable life choices.

title: Blind Spot Butler

tagline: For when you need a bike that's as unique as your aunt at a family reunion, Tarso Marques custom bikes are here. Imagine cruising down the street on a two-wheeler that's been tailored to your quirky tastes.

title: Escape the Suburbs... Eventually
tagline: So, your HOA banned golf carts, huh? And you're *this* close to perfecting that passive-aggressive garden gnome display? This scooter lets you extend your turf war to the next cul-de-sac over. Just imagine the looks on their faces as you silently glide past, judging their lawn care choices at 15mph.

title: Bike for the Utterly Lost
tagline: For when you're late to a dinner party in a flood zone, this three-speed folding bike is a lifesaver – or at least a dry-pants-saver.

title: Electric Cowboy Dreams (Nikola Badger)
tagline: For the rancher who's had it with gas stations, but still needs to haul hay and broken dreams.

title: Dad's Midlife Crisis Car
tagline: For when you need to relive the 70s, or impress your kid's soccer team with a gas-guzzler that's older than they are.
